comparator.name: Theology
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 regulations define a 180-ECTS Theology bachelor and four variants: with or without Greek, each with or without the PThU trajectory. The PThU trajectory with Greek is selected under the broad-academic-identity rule because it combines both biblical source languages with biblical, systematic, historical, intercultural and practical theology, and the current public programme page identifies it as the most commonly chosen variant. In Year 2 the PThU rules replace the ordinary media/text choice with Psychology and Sociology of Religion and replace Religion and Politics with Dogmatics. Year 3 is the prescribed 30-ECTS PThU block plus a specialization, Thesis Seminar, Science Communication and thesis. Origins of Religion: Foundational Texts and their Transformations is selected as the first specialization in official order, independently of UCR fit. The live programme page, current study-guide index and adopted regulations were rechecked on 2026-10-14; the settled route and curriculum remain unchanged. routeSelection.basis: The generic registry target names the Theology bachelor but no variant. The PThU trajectory with Greek is the broadest current theological pathway: it preserves both Hebrew and Greek and adds practical, dogmatic, historical, biblical, intercultural and ethical theology. The public programme page also presents it as the most commonly chosen variant. This selection is based on the target programme's academic identity and is independent of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Belief, cultural traditions & public life
alternatives.concept: Study questions of belief, meaning and the good life through philosophy, myth, literature, history, archaeology and visual heritage, then examine religious traditions' cultural and political contexts through sociology, psychology, law and politics. This is a related-fields programme, not a substitute for Christian theology, biblical languages, exegesis or pastoral formation.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines philosophy, history, literature and cultural interpretation with sociology, psychology, law and politics. The label describes those related fields and does not imply a Theology degree.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and seven level-300 courses. Introductory philosophy, history, literature, sociology, psychology, law and politics precede advanced historical, social-theory, conflict, heritage and interpretive work. Law, Society & Justice precedes Comparative Constitutional Law. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.

alternatives.label: Ethics of technology, health & planetary responsibility
alternatives.concept: Combine moral philosophy and human-rights reasoning with explicit AI ethics, biomedical and genetic foundations, human physiology and disease, sustainability governance, circular economy and renewable-system design. This responds to target-linked ethical questions about technology, genetic intervention, human life and climate through related disciplines rather than theological ethics.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum gives sustained and proportionate weight to moral philosophy, AI, biomedicine and genetics, and environmental governance and technology. The label does not claim theological ethics, medicine or engineering.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Life-science and sustainability gateway courses precede all dependent biomedical and sustainable-technology courses; philosophical foundations precede advanced work on mind, self and emotion. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.
alternatives.distinctness: Twenty courses, or 150 EC, differ in each direction. The first programme's history, literature, heritage, public-life and religion-adjacent social analysis are replaced by explicit AI ethics, molecular and physiological science, genetics and disease, sustainability governance, circular economy and renewable-system study. These changes are direct curricular consequences of the separate contemporary-ethics evidence, not threshold-filling substitutions.

candidates.label: Biblical languages, exegesis & confessional theology
candidates.assessment: The current Groningen curriculum independently confirms Hebrew, Greek, biblical texts and source-language exegesis. UCR has no Hebrew, Greek or Arabic acquisition sequence, biblical-studies progression, exegesis, dogmatics or theology-specific research environment. General literature, myth and heritage courses are already bounded contributions to the first programme and cannot sustain this direction.

candidates.label: Ministry, spiritual care & religious education
candidates.assessment: UCR can study ethics, health, psychology, institutions and communication, but it has no practical-theology, pastoral, supervised spiritual-care, church-leadership or teacher-training sequence. The absence of professional qualification is not the reason for rejection; the required religion-specific academic and practice formation is missing.

selection.assessment: The historical judgment correctly identified the absence of disciplinary theology, biblical languages and pastoral formation but applied a full-substitution threshold. One complete related-fields programme is defensible in belief, cultural traditions and public life, and the separately evidenced contemporary-ethics cluster supports a second complete and materially distinct programme. The next candidate—biblical languages, exegesis and confessional theology—is not feasible, so production stops at two. Ministry, spiritual care and religious education were also assessed and remain infeasible for missing religion-specific academic and practice formation.

blocks: Both examine fundamental questions about God, meaning and spirituality through philosophical argument; UCR does not provide the comparator's theology-specific framing.
Both interpret foundational narratives and their later transformations across cultures; UCR studies comparative myth and literature rather than biblical or theological source traditions.
Both develop ethical reasoning about responsibility and the good life; UCR teaches philosophical and applied ethics rather than theological ethics.
The comparator requires an independent Theology thesis; UCR optional independent research is shown separately and does not supply theology-specific sources, methods or supervision.

notes.text: The Groningen programme is a Theology degree built around Hebrew and Greek, biblical texts and exegesis, Christian thought, dogmatics, practical, historical, biblical, intercultural and ethical theology, and a Theology thesis. UCR can study belief, meaning, cultural traditions, public life and contemporary ethical questions through adjacent humanities, social sciences, biomedicine and sustainability, but neither UCR route reproduces the theological discipline.

UCR offers no biblical Hebrew or Greek, sustained scriptural exegesis, dogmatics, systematic or practical theology, pastoral formation, ministry preparation or supervised spiritual-care practice. The included programmes therefore remain bounded related-field responses.
